title: W4 fix incomplete: 'Form opened' timeline line still sorts out of chronological order whenever it shares a calendar day with an attempt batch — the sort compares raw mixed-format timestamps (PG ::text space vs RFC3339 'T'), and ' ' < 'T' lexically
evidence: view_attempt_summary prepends TimelineLine(form_opened, ts) then sorts by string.compare(a.at, b.at). Attempts `at` is RFC3339 with 'T' (server/src/reference_checks/sweep.gleam:180 timestamp.to_rfc3339, pinned '2026-08-01T10:04:00Z' in tests); form_opened_at is Postgres ::text with a space, pinned on the real wire by server/test/integration/reference_detail_payload_integration_test.gleam:307 ("form_opened_at":"2026-08-01 21:12:00+00"). Lexically, '2026-08-01 09:30:00+00' < '2026-08-01T09:00:00Z' (0x20 < 0x54) — verified empirically — so a form opened at 09:30 renders ABOVE an invitation sent at 09:00 the same day, and above a same-day reminder even when it opened after it (the exact W4 scenario). The W4 test (reference_panel_test.gleam:831) uses form_opened_at: Some("2026-08-03T18:00:00Z") — the RFC3339 form the server never sends — so CI cannot catch the misorder. normalize_datetime (the space->T swap) already exists for the datetime attribute but is not applied to the sort comparator.
detail: The r1 W4 fix claimed 'chronological by timestamp'; the sort is only chronological across different calendar days. Same-day form-open (the common case — referees open the invite link minutes/hours after the send) renders the mini timeline reversed. Fix: sort on normalize_datetime(line.at) (or normalize form_opened_at at the source), and pin the same-day case with the PG-space fixture format.

title: N2 fix incomplete: <time datetime> still carries a colon-less '+00' offset — '2026-08-01T21:12:00+00' is not a valid HTML datetime value
evidence: normalize_datetime swaps the space for 'T' but leaves the Postgres offset as '+00'. The HTML datetime grammar requires a time-zone offset of 'Z' or '+HH:MM' (colon mandatory); '2026-08-01T21:12:00+00' remains invalid — the same invalidity r1 N2 flagged, only the separator changed. The r1 N2 fix ('datetime normalized') is therefore partial.
detail: The datetime attribute on the Form-opened timeline line (and any PG ::text timestamp line) is still not a valid HTML datetime value. Browsers ignore invalid datetime attributes, so impact is validity/a11y-grade only — same severity as the r1 note.

title: W1 fix's second half missing: no_em_dash_test was NOT extended to scan refcheck copy — the claimed CI pin for the refcheck copy block did not land
evidence: no_em_dash_test still iterates for_each_copy = all_codes() x all_contexts() (toast/page codes only); grep of client/test/copy_test.gleam for 'refcheck' returns nothing. The r1 W1 recommended fix ('extend no_em_dash_test to scan refcheck copy') and the rework's claimed fix ('no_em_dash_test extended to scan refcheck consts') are not present. The two flagged em-dash strings themselves ARE fixed (refcheck_unmoderated_flag and refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed in client/src/copy.gleam now contain no em-dash — verified), so no live user-facing defect — but the RT CI em-dash ban still does not cover the ~40 new refcheck copy strings, so a future reintroduction ships green.
detail: Missing guard extension only; the actual r1 defect (two em-dashes in shipped strings) is fixed. Reported because the fix map explicitly claims the test extension landed.
